brief: Meta's new stock offering and Anthropic's upcoming IPO add to a surfeit of equity supply that poses a structural headwind for stocks. Net equity supply hit a record high above $150 billion in Q2. Since the late 1990s net equity supply has been negative almost every quarter, with buybacks and M&A outweighing secondary issuance and IPOs, but that pattern has flipped this year. Hyperscalers' perceived need for capital to build out compute capacity has pushed them toward more equity financing alongside debt issuance, as debt becomes more expensive. Unlisted firms increasingly want public-market funding, exemplified by Anthropic's IPO, which is set to eclipse SpaceX's record-sized summer offering. Buybacks continue as long as firms stay free-cash-flow positive after the capex uplift, but aggregate S&P 500 free cash flow is projected to fall given the scale of capex, which could crimp buyback plans and strengthen the equity-supply headwind.
